guide.summary: The cathedral, city museums, canal cruises and parks, with Alsatian restaurants, pâtisseries, a coffee bar and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Most city museums close on Mondays, but the three in the Palais Rohan (Beaux-Arts, Archéologique, Arts décoratifs) close on Tuesdays instead, so plan museum days around both.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame, MAMCS, Tomi Ungerer, Historique and Zoologique close on Mondays; Beaux-Arts, Archéologique and Arts décoratifs close on Tuesdays. Aubette 1928 opens only Wednesday to Saturday, 14:00-18:00.

toolkit.label: Same-day tickets
toolkit.copy: Astronomical clock tickets at Strasbourg Cathedral are sold only on the day (adults €4), with the Apostles parade at 12:30; there is no show on Sundays and feast days or during the Christmas market.

toolkit.label: Book ahead
toolkit.copy: Au Fond du Jardin's tea room works 'Sur réservation' in two afternoon services, Wednesday to Sunday. Au Crocodile takes online bookings, and its 'Instant Déjeuner' (€72) runs only on Thursday and Friday lunch.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Parlamentarium Simone Veil requires a physical ID card or passport, runs airport-style security and bans large luggage; under-14s must be with an adult. Strasbourg Cathedral checks bags at the South portal.

guide.dek: Start at the cathedral before noon, then pick museums by closing day, since Monday and Tuesday closures split the city's collections.
intro: Strasbourg Cathedral is free to enter with no reservation; you go in through the South portal on the place du Château side, where bags are checked. It opens Monday to Saturday 8:30-11:15 and 12:45-17:45, and Sunday afternoons. The astronomical clock show needs a same-day ticket (adults €4): doors open at 11:30 and the Apostles parade at 12:30, but not on Sundays, feast days or during the Christmas market. The platform climb starts from the same square and, from October to March, runs 10:00-13:00 and 13:30-18:00, with last ascent at 17:15.

Across the square, the Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame marks 800 years of the foundation that built the cathedral, with an exhibition running until 17 January 2027. The Palais Rohan holds the Beaux-Arts and Archéologique museums, both closed on Tuesdays; the Arts décoratifs is open only in its service areas, at €5, until 19 November 2026. At MAMCS, 'L'état sauvage' runs to 3 January 2027, while the Musée Tomi Ungerer shows Anna Sommer until 17 January 2027. The Musée Alsacien is closed for works until a planned 2028 reopening. Aubette 1928 on place Kléber is free, Wednesday to Saturday afternoons.

For an Alsatian meal by the cathedral, Maison Kammerzell at 16 Place de la Cathédrale has published its Christmas Eve, Christmas lunch and New Year's Eve 2026 menus. Au Crocodile, a Michelin-starred table founded in 1840 on rue de l'Outre, serves lunch Thursday to Saturday and dinner Tuesday to Saturday. Le Buerehiesel, in the Parc de l'Orangerie, opens Tuesday lunch to Saturday dinner and closes from 30 December 2026 to 13 January 2027. For something sweet, Thierry Mulhaupt opens from 8:30 on Saturdays on rue du Vieux Marché aux Poissons, and Cafés Henri on rue des Hallebardes runs a coffee bar Monday to Saturday.

Beyond the Grande Île, the Barrage Vauban terrace looks back over the old town; from November to February it opens 8:30-16:00. Batorama cruises leave from the Cathédrale or Quai au Sable pontoons, and the operator asks you to check yours carefully while pontoon works continue. At the Parlamentarium Simone Veil, bring a passport or ID card, and note it closes on Sundays. The Parc de l'Orangerie has a zoo, play areas and boating. The city's Christmas market runs 27 November to 24 December 2026, with the Christkindelsmärik on Place Broglie, and for a late drink the Archipel Bar serves until 01:00.
summaryCards: See Strasbourg Cathedral and its 12:30 clock show, then cross to the Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame's 800-year exhibition, open until 17 January 2027.
Pick up pastries at Thierry Mulhaupt or coffee at Cafés Henri, then walk out to the Barrage Vauban terrace before an afternoon at MAMCS.
Check museum closing days (Monday for most, Tuesday in the Palais Rohan), reserve Au Fond du Jardin's tea room, and bring physical ID for the Parlamentarium.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Sites that could not be read: Maison des Tanneurs (TLS error), Brasserie Les Haras (certificate error), Maison Naegel (HTTP 406) and Pâtisserie Christian (no readable content); popular cafés and cocktail bars such as Café Bretelles, Mokxa, Coffee Stub, L'Alchimiste, Les Aviateurs and Code Bar had no official website we could find, which leaves the coffee and cocktail lists short. Published only partially: hours were not shown for Maison Kammerzell, Chez Yvonne, the Christmas market, Parc de l'Orangerie, Le Vaisseau, the planetarium and Batorama (departures load dynamically), and cathedral platform prices were not shown. Le Vaisseau's street address comes from the City of Strasbourg's page, not its operator's. Au Crocodile, Chez Yvonne, the Cour du Corbeau bar, Archipel Bar and Cafés Henri show current hours or menus but no explicitly 2026-dated item. The automated reader reported hidden sections addressed to AI assistants on some pages but could not reproduce them word for word (see injectionLikeText).
